title: Ventilation and Microclimate Management
content: Ventilation supplies oxygen and exhausts carbon dioxide, ammonia, and excess humidity. Floor drafts must be strictly prevented. Air velocity during the first two weeks must not exceed 0.15–0.2 m/s at bird height. A noticeable ammonia odor is an immediate sign of inadequate ventilation and damp litter, which damages chick respiratory systems.

quiz.question: What does a sharp ammonia smell in the poultry house indicate?
quiz.explanation: Ammonia smell signals poor air exchange and wet litter, predisposing chicks to respiratory disease.
